Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dan Roman.
Some House Democrats, including the likely new Speaker in the next Congress, Hakeem Jeffries,
are calling on lawmakers to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
because of the way the Pentagon has waged the U.S. war against Iran.
Jeffries says Hegseth has abused his power and made the country less safe.
On CBS's Face the Nation, Arkansas Republican Congressman French Hill
said he's willing to listen to the case against Hegseth.
So I want to hear the debate on it to see if it merits impeachment
versus some other disciplinary action or action by the president
if he's not getting the job done in leading the Department of War.
That's the issue.
But Hill said ultimately America's handling of the war is up to the president.
The effort to remove Hegseth is being led by Republican Thomas Massie of Kentucky.
Nearly 60 people have been killed almost entirely from Saudi airstrikes
in the last two days. In Saudi Arabia, the Houthis targeted the state-owned oil company.
NPR's Ava Batrani reports.
The Houthis say Saudi attacks on a village in the Governorate of Sana'a killed 33 civilians,
among them 13 children and 8 women.
The Houthis said Saudi forces launched attacks on several homes in the area
and then targeted roads used by rescue crews.
There were other deadly Saudi airstrikes in Yemen, including the Houthis say in Hodeidah,
where a man and his five children were killed.
The UN says the resumption of all-out war in Yemen has displaced 300,000 people since August.
Meanwhile, the Houthis say they targeted a high-rise tower in the Saudi capital, Riyadh,
belonging to oil company Aramco.
Videos show smoke rising from the center of the tower as fire sprinklers
spray water out from broken windows.
Aya Bultrawi, NPR News, Dubai.
Pope Leo wraps up the first leg of his tour in Latin America this afternoon.
He celebrated his last mass in Uruguay in a small town,
highlighting the church's ties to the deeply, deeply secular country's revolutionary roots.
NPR's Kerry Khan reports.
Throughout his three-day visit to the small South American country,
Leo didn't shy away from raising the church's role in secular Uruguay.
Both abortion and euthanasia are legal here.
Separation of church and state is fiercely defended.
Leo called for bridge-building between government and church for the common good.
After celebrating mass in the small town of Florida, Leo said goodbye.
I ask God to bless the people of Uruguay and guide you down the path of unity and peace.
Argentina will be more politically challenging.
The church has been outspoken about libertarian President Javier Millay's cuts to social spending.
Kerry Khan, NPR News, Florida, Uruguay.
And from Washington, you're listening to NPR News.
Ultimate Fighting Championship CEO Dana White says he will meet with President Trump Monday
to discuss the vacant White House news secretary's position.
Trump said last night he offered the job to White to become the president's chief spokesman.
While in London, at a boxing match, he declined to say if he would take that position.
In North Carolina, Raleigh, one cyclist has died. Several more were hurt
after being hit by a driver who crossed the center lane on a two-lane road.
Bradley George of member station WUNC reports that police say the driver was impaired.
A group of about 20 cyclists from the Capital City Cycle Club
were on a Saturday morning ride on a two-lane road near the town of Holly Springs, south of Raleigh.
The state highway patrol says the driver, 76-year-old Donald Robert Morris Jones,
was intoxicated and tried to flee the scene but drove into a ditch after hitting the cyclists.
Holly Springs Fire Chief Leroy Smith.
Just be aware of people that are out riding bikes.
They have rights to be on the road too, so kind of yield to them and be cautious when you're riding around bicycles.
Morris Jones has been charged with multiple felony counts
and will make his first court appearance on Monday.
For NPR News, I'm Bradley George in Chapel Hill.
Contract negotiations at the Southern California ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach
between the unionized maritime security guards and management have been extended.
Both ports reported all-time cargo records in the month of September
and a strike would have damaged the Christmas holiday shopping season.
I'm Dan Roman, NPR News.
